title: Hollywood's most beautiful woman... secretly invented the idea in your Bluetooth
note: True story: Hedy Lamarr, US Patent 2,292,387 (1942) with George Antheil. Her own voice: Fleming Meeks's 1990 Forbes tapes (PBS American Masters, aLPqLCtkkTk) and the Bombshell trailer. Newsreel: British Movietone war bonds (1942). Never 'she invented WiFi'. No Ecstasy footage. Script: hedy_lamarr.script.md.

beats.say: Hollywood called her the most beautiful woman in the world. But she was secretly an inventor, and the idea she patented is inside your Bluetooth.
Her name was Hedwig Kiesler, from Vienna. At eighteen, she starred in a film so daring it was banned in several countries.
That same year, she married Fritz Mandl, an arms dealer who supplied Mussolini. He reportedly tried to buy up every copy of her film.
By her account, he kept her like a prisoner. She sat silently through his business dinners, listening to men talk about weapons.
In 1937, she escaped. Accounts differ, but by her own telling, she slipped out disguised as her maid.
beats.speak: In nineteen thirty-seven, she escaped. Accounts differ, but by her own telling, she slipped out disguised as her maid.

beats.say: She talked her way onto the ocean liner carrying MGM boss Louis B. Mayer, and stepped off with a contract, and a new name. Hedy Lamarr.
Hollywood sold her as the most beautiful woman in the world.
And at night, she invented. When World War Two began, she wanted to stop enemies from jamming the radio signals that guided torpedoes.
With composer George Antheil, she came up with an idea. Make the signal hop between frequencies, synced like two player pianos.
beats.speak: With composer George Antile, she came up with an idea. Make the signal hop between frequencies, synced like two player pianos.

beats.say: In 1942, they got a patent. Number 2,292,387. A Secret Communication System.
beats.speak: In nineteen forty-two, they got a patent. Number two, two nine two, three eight seven. A Secret Communication System.

beats.say: The Navy shelved it, and suggested she'd help more by selling war bonds. So she did.
By one account, she raised seven million dollars in a single night. But from her invention, she never made a cent. Twenty years later, Navy ships were using frequency hopping.
To be fair, she didn't invent WiFi, and she wasn't the first to imagine frequency hopping. But her patent showed how to make it work, decades before anyone used it.
In 1997, she finally got an award for it. Her reaction: It's about time.
beats.speak: In nineteen ninety-seven, she finally got an award for it. Her reaction: It's about time.

beats.say: She died in 2000. In 2014, she was inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame.
beats.speak: She died in two thousand. In twenty fourteen, she was inducted into the National Inventors Hall of Fame.

beats.say: So next time your Bluetooth connects, remember. Hollywood's most beautiful woman thought of it first.

credits: PBS American Masters (Bombshell: The Hedy Lamarr Story, 2017)
